definitions.meaning: A special feature of a living thing that helps it survive in its home: a thick stem, camouflage colours or a long migration journey.
Blending in with your home: the moth's wings match the tree bark, so hungry birds cannot spot it.
The long yearly journey some birds make: flying thousands of kilometres to warmer places for winter and returning in spring.
The place where a living thing lives, which gives it food and shelter: a desert, a tree or a forest.
To stay alive in your home: a living thing survives when its features help it find food and water and stay safe.
The many groups of parents and young over a very long time: features develop slowly over many, many generations, not overnight.

mechanismSteps: Watch out: features are not grown by choice: the cactus in the hot, dry desert has a thick stem that stores water like a bottle, sharp thorns that stop thirsty animals biting it, and deep roots that find water - and none of these features was grown by choice.
Blending in keeps animals safe: the moth's wings are the same colour as the tree bark, so it blends into its home and hungry birds fly right past without seeing it.
Birds travel far to survive: when winter comes and food is hard to find, the birds fly thousands of kilometres to warmer places, then return when spring brings food back.
People change animal homes: when people clear forests to build farms and roads, the trees go and the animals that lived there lose their food and shelter.
objectives: Name the features that help a cactus survive in a hot, dry desert
Explain how camouflage keeps an animal safe from hungry birds
Explain why birds migrate and when they return
Say why animal features are not chosen on purpose, and what happens when people clear a forest
subject: science
title: Adaptations: built to survive

trap.explanation: The feature fits the animal so well that it looks chosen on purpose. These features did not appear overnight: they developed over many, many generations, not by choice. In the animation scene s1 the warning is in the caption itself - features are not grown by choice - so admire how well the feature fits without saying the animal chose it.
trap.misconception: An animal can decide to grow a new feature when it needs one.

workedExample: In scene s1, follow the cactus as a worked example: its thick stem stores water like a bottle for the dry days, its sharp thorns stop thirsty animals from biting it, and its deep roots reach down to find water. Each feature is a check: name the feature, name the desert problem it solves - no water, thirsty animals, dry sand - then say how it helps the cactus survive.
